teams.body: The Fiji men's senior international side secured the biggest win of their last 11 games with a 63-10 home victory against Canada in September 2025 during the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage. teams.heading: England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg stretchered off in Bristol victory
teams.body: England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg was stretchered off during Bristol’s 41-26 victory over Northampton on Saturday. The midfielder required an eight-minute stoppage for treatment after a collision with Henry Pollock left him knocked out. While Bristol secured a bonus-point win, the focus turned to the severity of the incident as the player was carried from the pitch. There is no further update on his condition following the conclusion of the weekend's Premiership fixtures.

teams.heading: Ireland women seal seven-try win over Japan in Cork fixture
teams.body: The Ireland women’s side secured a comprehensive 43-19 victory over Japan at Virgin Media Park on Saturday. After recovering from an early deficit, the hosts dominated proceedings with seven tries, including efforts from Eilis Cahill, Brittany Hogan, and a record-extending 25th international try for Beibhinn Parsons. Debuting replacements Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett also crossed the whitewash late in the contest. Scott Bemand’s squad now carries this momentum into their upcoming two-match series against South Africa in the WXV.

teams.heading: Japan Sakura XV women's side suffer comprehensive defeat to Ireland
teams.body: The Japan Sakura XV women's side fell to a 43-19 defeat against Ireland in Cork on Saturday. Despite an early try from Sakurako Korai, the visitors were unable to contain Ireland’s attacking threat, conceding seven tries in total. While Japan showed glimpses of their established rolling maul strength with a second-half score from Nijiho Nagata, the side was hampered by a high penalty count and a late yellow card, marking the end of their two-match series in Ireland.

teams.heading: Andre Esterhuizen captains Sharks as Springboks return for Leinster fixture
teams.body: The Sharks have welcomed back several returning Springboks for their United Rugby Championship clash against Leinster in Durban. Andre Esterhuizen will captain the side from inside centre after recently leading the national team in Australia. Head coach JP Pietersen also named Thomas du Toit at loosehead prop for his second debut for the club following his stint with Bath. World Cup winners Ox Nche and Eben Etzebeth feature among the replacements as the Durban outfit opts for a traditional five-three split on the bench.
